summary: This standards-track document specifies algorithm identifiers and ASN.1 encoding formats for elliptic curve constructs using curve25519 and curve448 in X.509. It covers the Ed25519 and Ed448 signature algorithms and the X25519 and X448 key agreement algorithms, including public and private key encodings.

plainLanguage.summary: This RFC assigns standard identifiers to four cryptographic algorithms and explains how their keys and signatures fit into X.509 structures. The rules help different systems represent the same algorithm consistently.

subtitle: Defines X.509 identifiers and encodings for Ed25519, Ed448, X25519 and X448.

tldr.problem: X.509 certificates need standard identifiers and encodings for the curve25519 and curve448 signature and key-agreement algorithms.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC defines four object identifiers, requires absent parameters and specifies public-key, private-key and signature encodings.
tldr.outcome: Implementations can represent these keys and signatures consistently in X.509. RFC 9295 later updates this RFC.

today: RFC 8410 is a Proposed Standard and is updated by RFC 9295.

sections.title: Algorithms Covered by the RFC
sections.content:
Curve25519 and curve448 can be used for Diffie-Hellman key agreement and digital signatures. The key-agreement names are X25519 and X448. Ed25519 and Ed448 identify the PureEdDSA signature mode.

This RFC defines object identifiers and encoding rules for those four algorithms. It does not define the prehash variants of EdDSA or the use of EdDSA contexts.
sections.plainLanguage: The document covers two key-agreement algorithms and two signature algorithms. It gives them identifiers and encoding rules for X.509 use.

sections.title: Algorithm Identifiers
sections.content:
An X.509 AlgorithmIdentifier contains an object identifier and optional parameters. This RFC defines identifiers for X25519, X448, Ed25519 and Ed448. Parameters must be absent for all four identifiers.

The identifiers apply to public keys and private keys, and the EdDSA identifiers also apply to signatures. Systems that require parameters should be fixed or isolated rather than extending that requirement to other systems.
sections.plainLanguage: Each algorithm gets a numeric identifier. For these identifiers, no parameter value follows the identifier.

sections.title: Public Keys and Key Usage
sections.content:
In a certificate, SubjectPublicKeyInfo contains the algorithm identifier and a BIT STRING holding the public-key bytes. These algorithms encode public keys as whole bytes. The public key is computed differently for Diffie-Hellman and EdDSA, so the same private key does not produce the same public key for both.

If a certificate includes a keyUsage extension, X25519 and X448 require keyAgreement. End-entity Ed25519 and Ed448 certificates require digitalSignature, nonRepudiation or both; certification-authority certificates have additional allowed uses.
sections.plainLanguage: The certificate stores the algorithm identifier beside the public key. Its key-usage field states what the key is allowed to do.

sections.title: Signatures and Private-Key Encoding
sections.content:
EdDSA signatures use the same algorithm identifier as the corresponding public key, with parameters absent. The signature bytes are placed directly in the certificate's signature BIT STRING without extra ASN.1 wrapping.

A private key uses the OneAsymmetricKey structure. The private-key bytes are wrapped in a CurvePrivateKey OCTET STRING and then in the privateKey field; a publicKey field may also be present.
sections.plainLanguage: The signature bytes go directly into the signature field. A private key is stored inside the specified nested byte-string structure.

sections.title: Names, Examples and Invalid Encodings
sections.content:
The RFC recommends consistent readable names: use X25519 or X448 when the curve is known, and ECDH when it is not. For signatures, use Ed25519 or Ed448 when known and EdDSA when the curve is not known or relevant.

Examples show an Ed25519 public key, an X25519 certificate signed with Ed25519 and Ed25519 private keys. Appendix A describes invalid key encodings, including malformed ASN.1, keys that violate curve formatting rules and mismatched public and private keys.
sections.plainLanguage: The RFC includes sample public keys, certificates and private keys. It also lists errors an importer must detect when reading an encoded key.

sections.title: Security and Registry Notes
sections.content:
The security considerations of RFC 5280, RFC 7748 and RFC 8032 apply. The RFC emphasizes that ECDH and EdDSA compute public keys differently, so one public key cannot serve both uses.

IANA assigned value 93 to the ASN.1 module identifier id-mod-safecurves-pkix. The four algorithm object identifiers are registered separately.
sections.plainLanguage: Do not use one public key for both key agreement and signing. The algorithms derive their public keys differently.
